content.content:
AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'
Transform: AWS::Serverless-2016-10-31
Description: >
  TLDR backend (app stack) — HTTP API v2 + Google JWT authorizer, one Lambda, DynamoDB single table.

Parameters:
  GoogleClientId:
    Type: String
    # Intentionally no default: an empty JWT-authorizer audience would accept ID tokens minted for
    # ANY Google app. This MUST be the Google Cloud OAuth "Web application" client id.
    Description: Google OAuth "Web application" client id — the JWT authorizer audience (also the extension's auth client_id).
    AllowedPattern: '.+'
    ConstraintDescription: GoogleClientId must be provided.
  AllowedExtensionOrigin:
    Type: String
    Default: '*'
    Description: >
      CORS allowed origin. Keep '*': API Gateway HTTP API v2 REJECTS the chrome-extension:// scheme in CORS
      AllowOrigins ("Invalid format for origin"), so the extension origin can't be set here. Not a security
      gap — writes are gated by the JWT authorizer and reads are public; the '*' is also what lets the
      extension reach the API under standard CORS (so it needs no host_permissions). The security boundary is
      the JWT authorizer, never browser CORS. (See dev/docs/architecture.md §6.3 / §12-A9 / §12-A10.)
  RateLimitPerMinute:
    Type: Number
    Default: 10
    Description: Max comments one author may post per minute (enforced by a TTL'd DynamoDB counter). 0 disables.
  MaxBodyBytes:
    Type: Number
    Default: 8192
  QueryLimit:
    Type: Number
    Default: 50
  EmailHashSalt:
    Type: String
    Default: ''
    NoEcho: true
    Description: >
      Server secret salting the stored one-way email hash (used for moderation only; the hash is never
      returned). Set to a long random string; rotating it disconnects old hashes from new ones.

Conditions:
  # Which environment this is, is derived from the STACK NAME — not an external parameter. Production
  # is the one canonical stack named `tldr-app`; its table name is then pinned (below) to the exact
  # legacy `tldr-comments`. Nothing passed at deploy time can make prod point at a different table.
  # Any other stack name (tldr-app-dev, or an ad-hoc tldr-app-<x>) is non-prod and gets its own
  # stack-scoped table, so dev/sandbox testing can never read or write prod data.
  IsProd: !Equals [!Ref AWS::StackName, tldr-app]

Globals:
  Function:
    Runtime: nodejs22.x
    Architectures:
      - x86_64
    Timeout: 10
    MemorySize: 256
    Environment:
      Variables:
        NODE_OPTIONS: --enable-source-maps
        TABLE_NAME: !Ref CommentsTable
        MAX_BODY_BYTES: !Ref MaxBodyBytes
        QUERY_LIMIT: !Ref QueryLimit
        RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE: !Ref RateLimitPerMinute
        EMAIL_HASH_SALT: !Ref EmailHashSalt

Resources:
  CommentsTable:
    Type: AWS::DynamoDB::Table
    # The one irreplaceable-state resource. Retain on delete AND on replace; PITR for restore-to-second.
    DeletionPolicy: Retain
    UpdateReplacePolicy: Retain
    Properties:
      # prod (stack tldr-app) => the exact legacy name, HARD-CODED in source so it can't be overridden
      # from outside (renaming would REPLACE the table — see UpdateReplacePolicy and the frozen-KeySchema
      # note below). Any other stack => a stack-scoped table (e.g. tldr-app-dev => tldr-app-dev-comments),
      # so it's physically distinct from prod's data store.
      TableName: !If [IsProd, tldr-comments, !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-comments']
      BillingMode: PAY_PER_REQUEST
      # FROZEN: editing the base table's KeySchema / AttributeDefinitions for pageId/commentId REPLACES
      # the table — a new EMPTY table; the data does NOT follow. Treat any changeset showing
      # "Replacement: True" here as a hard stop. Adding a GSI (below) is a separate, additive
      # UpdateTable operation — it does NOT touch the base KeySchema and does not replace the table.
      AttributeDefinitions:
        - AttributeName: pageId
          AttributeType: S
        - AttributeName: commentId
          AttributeType: S
        - AttributeName: categoryPageId
          AttributeType: S
        - AttributeName: voteCount
          AttributeType: N
      KeySchema:
        - AttributeName: pageId
          KeyType: HASH
        - AttributeName: commentId
          KeyType: RANGE
      # Issue #26 (link-hover preview): "the leading comment for pageId+category" needs a query the
      # base table can't answer (its only key is pageId+commentId, sorted by creation time, not votes).
      # `categoryPageId` (= "<pageId>#<category>") is written ONLY on comment items (handler.mjs), so
      # this GSI is naturally SPARSE — vote items and rate-limit counters never carry it and so never
      # appear here. `voteCount` already updates atomically via the existing vote TransactWriteItems
      # (handleVote), so the GSI tracks it with no new write path. A Query keyed on categoryPageId with
      # ScanIndexForward=false, Limit=1 returns the top-voted comment; ties (equal top voteCount) break
      # arbitrarily (DynamoDB's tie order, not a documented contract) — acceptable for a "leading
      # comment" preview. KNOWN LIMITATION: a GSI only indexes items that already carry its key
      # attributes, so comments written BEFORE this shipped are invisible to this index until rewritten
      # — there is no backfill (dev/docs/architecture.md §5.3).
      GlobalSecondaryIndexes:
        - IndexName: CategoryRankIndex
          KeySchema:
            - AttributeName: categoryPageId
              KeyType: HASH
            - AttributeName: voteCount
              KeyType: RANGE
          Projection:
            ProjectionType: ALL
      PointInTimeRecoverySpecification:
        PointInTimeRecoveryEnabled: true
      # Per-author rate-limit counter items carry an `expiresAt` (epoch seconds) and self-delete.
      # Real comment items have no such attribute, so TTL never touches them.
      TimeToLiveSpecification:
        AttributeName: expiresAt
        Enabled: true
      SSESpecification:
        SSEEnabled: true

  CommentsApi:
    Type: AWS::Serverless::HttpApi
    Properties:
      # API Gateway answers the CORS preflight (OPTIONS) itself, unauthenticated, before routing.
      CorsConfiguration:
        AllowOrigins:
          - !Ref AllowedExtensionOrigin
        AllowMethods:
          - GET
          - POST
          # DELETE is the vote toggle-off (RemoveVote, issue #22). Without it here the browser's
          # preflight for a DELETE gets no Access-Control-Allow-Origin and un-voting fails with a CORS
          # error ("No 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin' header… / Failed to fetch") — visible only in a
          # real browser, never in a unit test.
          - DELETE
          - OPTIONS
        AllowHeaders:
          - authorization
          - content-type
          # The client attaches X-Client-Version (version telemetry, issue #29) to every request. A
          # custom header makes even the public GET a non-simple request, so the browser preflights
          # it — this MUST list the header or the preflight fails and reads/posts break in-browser.
          - x-client-version
        MaxAge: 600
      Auth:
        Authorizers:
          GoogleJwt:
            IdentitySource: $request.header.Authorization
            JwtConfiguration:
              issuer: https://accounts.google.com
              audience:
                - !Ref GoogleClientId
        # No DefaultAuthorizer: routes opt in. GET /comments stays PUBLIC — reads are public by
        # design (a community-notes product; every viewer sees the same list). Writes are gated.

  CommentsFunction:
    Type: AWS::Serverless::Function
    Properties:
      CodeUri: ./
      # The esbuild builder writes a single entry point to <artifact>/handler.js (the src/ prefix is
      # stripped — esbuild's default outbase is the entry's own dir), so the Handler is handler.handler.
      Handler: handler.handler
      Events:
        PostComment:
          Type: HttpApi
          Properties:
            ApiId: !Ref CommentsApi
            Method: POST
            Path: /comments
            Auth:
              Authorizer: GoogleJwt
        GetComments:
          Type: HttpApi
          Properties:
            ApiId: !Ref CommentsApi
            Method: GET
            Path: /comments
            # No Auth => public read.
        GetTopComment:
          Type: HttpApi
          Properties:
            ApiId: !Ref CommentsApi
            Method: GET
            Path: /comments/top
            # No Auth => public read, same as GetComments (issue #26, the CategoryRankIndex GSI above).
        CastVote:
          Type: HttpApi
          Properties:
            ApiId: !Ref CommentsApi
            Method: POST
            Path: /comments/{commentId}/vote
            Auth:
              Authorizer: GoogleJwt
        RemoveVote:
          Type: HttpApi
          Properties:
            ApiId: !Ref CommentsApi
            Method: DELETE
            Path: /comments/{commentId}/vote
            Auth:
              Authorizer: GoogleJwt
      Policies:
        - Statement:
            - Effect: Allow
              # Voting writes two items in one TransactWriteItems (the vote item + the comment's
              # voteCount); a toggle-off deletes the vote item. DynamoDB authorizes a transaction by
              # its UNDERLYING per-item actions (there is no dynamodb:TransactWriteItems action), so
              # PutItem/UpdateItem/DeleteItem together cover both votes and posts. (issue #22)
              Action:
                - dynamodb:PutItem
                - dynamodb:Query
                - dynamodb:UpdateItem
                - dynamodb:DeleteItem
              # A GSI Query is authorized against the INDEX's own ARN, not just the table's (issue #26,
              # GetTopComment querying CategoryRankIndex) — the table ARN alone is insufficient for that.
              Resource:
                - !GetAtt CommentsTable.Arn
                - !Sub '${CommentsTable.Arn}/index/CategoryRankIndex'
    Metadata:
      BuildMethod: esbuild
      BuildProperties:
        EntryPoints:
          - src/handler.mjs
        Target: node22
        Format: cjs
        Minify: true
        Sourcemap: true
        # Bundle the AWS SDK: the managed runtime does NOT ship @aws-sdk/lib-dynamodb, and its
        # @aws-sdk minor drifts across runtime patches. Bundling makes the artifact deterministic.
        External: []

  # Pre-create the log group so we own its retention (Lambda's auto-created group never expires).
  CommentsFunctionLogGroup:
    Type: AWS::Logs::LogGroup
    DeletionPolicy: Retain
    UpdateReplacePolicy: Retain
    Properties:
      LogGroupName: !Sub /aws/lambda/${CommentsFunction}
      RetentionInDays: 30

Outputs:
  ApiUrl:
    Description: Base URL for the API. Clients POST/GET <ApiUrl>/comments.
    Value: !Sub https://${CommentsApi}.execute-api.${AWS::Region}.amazonaws.com
  CommentsTableName:
    Value: !Ref CommentsTable

The page body is the caller's PRIVACY.md verbatim — the single source # of truth, no duplicated copy. # # Deliberately NOT Chrome-specific (hence the unprefixed name): any publish # standard whose store listing needs a live privacy-policy URL deploys through # it. Vendored into the extension repo by the chrome-extension-release pack; # workflow_call ONLY. It is invoked by "Chrome extension: Publish to Chrome Web # Store" (uses: ./.github/workflows/deploy-privacy-page.yml) so the page is # refreshed whenever the listing ships (and, because that publish workflow runs # this leg even when the upload leg fails, it's also how the /privacy/ URL first # goes live before the first publication). There is no standalone privacy # dispatch stub — a repo never calls this directly. # # One-time owner setup in the calling repo: Pages source = "GitHub Actions" # (repo Settings → Pages). Production deploys only from the default branch (the # github-pages environment's branch policy), so the calling stub must be on # `main` to publish. # # The calling job must grant `permissions: contents: read, pages: write, # id-token: write, issues: write` (Pages deploy + the failure reporter). name: Deploy privacy policy to GitHub Pages (reusable) on: workflow_call: inputs: privacy_md_path: description: "Repo-relative path of the privacy policy Markdown" required: false type: string default: dev/build/release/store_artifacts/PRIVACY.md # Least privilege for a Pages deploy: read the repo, write Pages, mint the OIDC # token deploy-pages exchanges. permissions: contents: read pages: write id-token: write # Never run two Pages deploys at once; let an in-flight deploy finish. concurrency: group: pages cancel-in-progress: false jobs: build: runs-on: ubuntu-latest steps: - uses: actions/checkout@v5 - name: Assemble the Pages site from PRIVACY.md run: | set -euo pipefail mkdir -p site # The policy page: a permalink pins the public path; the body is # PRIVACY.md verbatim (single source of truth — no duplicated copy). { printf -- '---\npermalink: /privacy/\ntitle: "Privacy Policy"\n---\n\n' cat "${{ inputs.privacy_md_path }}" } > site/privacy.md # Site root redirects to the policy (relative link → no baseurl to hardcode). printf '%s\n' \ '' \ '' \ '' \ 'Privacy Policy' \ 'Privacy Policy' > site/index.html - uses: actions/configure-pages@v5 - uses: actions/jekyll-build-pages@v1 with: source: ./site destination: ./_site - uses: actions/upload-pages-artifact@v3 deploy: needs: build runs-on: ubuntu-latest environment: name: github-pages url: ${{ steps.deployment.outputs.page_url }} steps: - id: deployment uses: actions/deploy-pages@v4 # A standalone (dispatch-stub) Pages deploy is unattended — a failure just # turns the run red. Surface it as a tracking issue. The job-level permission # below is what the token actually carries (the top-level block above omits # issues on purpose); the caller grants issues:write through its call. report-failure: needs: [build, deploy] if: failure() runs-on: ubuntu-latest permissions: issues: write steps: - uses: ./.github/actions/report-failure with: workflow: "Deploy privacy policy to GitHub Pages"

content.content:
# AWS SAM — lessons

Notes for the `server/` backend: the SAM app stack (`template.yaml`). Portable subsets would propagate
to the corpus separately.

- **To talk to AWS from a session, use the AWS CLI (or a boto3 script) — there is no Claude/MCP tool for AWS.**
  The only connected MCP server is GitHub; a tool search for AWS turns up nothing. So checking a stack's real
  state is a plain CLI call, e.g. `aws cloudformation describe-stacks --stack-name tldr-app-dev --region
  il-central-1 --query "Stacks[0].StackStatus"` (dev stack is `tldr-app-dev`, prod is `tldr-app`; dev and prod
  live in separate accounts — see `dev/docs/dev-account-runbook.md` for the account/role details). This is the
  authoritative live status — the last-green
  `deploy.yml` run only tells you the last *deploy*, not the current stack state. The `.github/workflows/aws-status.yml`
  workflow is a read-only alternative but describes only `tldr-app` by name, so it won't target
  `tldr-app-dev` directly. Portable subset for the corpus (`claudinite-lesson` handoff): *AWS access is CLI/boto3,
  not an MCP tool.*

- **The AWS CLI is not pre-installed on the web/cloud runner — declare it in the environment setup script.**
  Cloud sessions start without `aws` (and without `boto3`/`sam`) on PATH, so a stack-status check needs a
  one-time install first: `pip install awscli` (a few seconds) or the official
  `awscli-exe-linux-x86_64.zip` bundle. The durable fix is one line in the **environment's setup script**
  (Claude Code on the web config — *not* a repo file; the `.claude/settings.json` `SessionStart` hooks here only
  sync Claudinite). Dev-account credentials (`AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID`/`AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`, `AWS_DEFAULT_REGION`)
  and `AWS_CA_BUNDLE=[REDACTED:env:NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS]` (so the CLI trusts the agent proxy) are already present in the
  env. Portable subset for the corpus (`claudinite-lesson` handoff): *pre-install the AWS CLI via the environment
  setup script; it is absent by default.*
############ WORKING INSTRUCTIONS
# TLDR — working instructions

The single entry-point for getting productive in this repo: set it up, change it, verify a change, and
ship it, without reverse-engineering the tree first. This is the **project-specific** layer — the
general working discipline (problem-first, the issue→branch→PR lifecycle, warnings-are-errors) is
auto-injected from the Claudinite corpus at session start (vendored at [`.claudinite/shared/`](../../.claudinite/shared/));
this doc restates none of it and instead links where a rule already lives.

Routing index, not a payload: read the linked doc when its trigger fires. For the lessons that layer on
top of the technology packs, [`CLAUDE.md`](CLAUDE.md) in this folder is the router.

## What TLDR is

Community tl;dr notes for any web page: a signed-in user reads and posts short notes ("comments")
attached to a page, keyed by its normalized URL. It is a **monorepo** composing two deployable
artifacts joined by one shared rule:

- **`extension/`** — an MV3 Chrome extension (side panel, no bundler; Chrome loads the ES modules directly). UI-facing. Its unit tests live in the sibling `extension-test/`.
- **`server/`** — an AWS serverless backend (SAM: HTTP API v2 + Google-JWT authorizer, one Lambda, DynamoDB). One CloudFormation stack (app).
- **`shared/`** — the single source of truth for URL→`pageId` normalization and category constants, vendored byte-identically into both sides and drift-guarded.

Trust boundary: **public reads; authenticated writes** (Google ID token → JWT authorizer, POST only). The as-built design and every decision's rationale live in [`dev/docs/architecture.md`](../docs/architecture.md); the top-level map is the [README](../../README.md).

## Set up from a clean clone

- **Runtime:** Node ≥ 22 (`node --test` / `node --check` are the whole toolchain — no bundler, no linter). Deploying the backend also needs the AWS SAM CLI + AWS credentials; developing the extension needs only Chrome.
- **Per-package installs are independent** — each sub-package has its own `package.json`/lockfile; there is no root `node_modules`. The root, `extension/`, and `shared/` need **no** dependencies at all; only `server/` and `dev/` do.

```bash
npm test                                       # root: URL-normalizer corpus + shared drift guard (no deps)
npm --prefix server ci && npm --prefix server test   # handler logic, DynamoDB mocked at the SDK boundary
npm --prefix extension test                    # extension unit (in extension-test/) + manifest/packaging guards (no deps)
npm --prefix dev ci && npm --prefix dev test         # the executable-requirements suite (extension UI + server)
```

`npm run test:all` (from the root) chains all four in order — that is the single command that must be green (see [Verify a change](#verify-a-change)).

> **The Claudinite mount.** The Claudinite corpus is **vendored** — tracked files under the shared
> mount, refreshed by the fleet's nightly maintenance (provenance stamped in
> `.claudinite-checks.json`). Nothing is fetched at session start; treat the vendored corpus as read-only.

## Run it / see it work

- **Extension, unpacked:** `chrome://extensions` → enable Developer mode → **Load unpacked** → select `extension/`. A plain checkout is **dev-pointed** (the committed `extension/config.mjs` `API_BASE_URL` targets the dev stack on purpose — a non-release build never talks to prod). Open the side panel from the toolbar; it fetches comments only while open, for the active tab, on commentable pages. Details + the dev/prod injection model: [`dev/docs/extension.md`](../docs/extension.md).
- **Server:** iterate against the **dev** stack (`tldr-app-dev`, its own DynamoDB table — a dev write can never reach prod). Deploy/seed commands and the dev-vs-prod promotion model: [`server/README.md`](../../server/README.md); the separate dev AWS account is the [dev-account runbook](../docs/dev-account-runbook.md).
- **See a *change* actually work — executable requirements.** A product requirement is stated once in [`dev/requirements/requirements.md`](../requirements/requirements.md) and proven by a case (a rendered-panel snapshot, a click-behavior test, or a pure rule). This is how a UI or server-contract change is *observed*, not just compiled. After an **intentional** panel change, regenerate the goldens: `npm --prefix dev run refresh:ui`. Method + invariants: [`dev/requirements/README.md`](../requirements/README.md) and the portable [ui-testing-guideline](../docs/ui-testing-guideline.md).

## Verify a change

- **Green means `npm run test:all` passes** — the same jobs CI runs (the `test: extension` and `test: requirements` workflows, plus the root drift guard). Reading CI to gate a merge: use the PR-scoped check state, not the run-listing tools — see [`ci-cd.md`](ci-cd.md).
- **The test bar:** every requirement is backed by a proof, and the suite goes red the moment a leaf is added to `requirements.md` without a case claiming it. Match the existing kind for the change (snapshot / behavior / logic). General test discipline (see-it-fail, snapshot rules) is the corpus `writing-tests` skill.
- **The expected is owner-owned — never edit an expected (or weaken an assertion) to turn a red requirement green.** On a mismatch, surface *actual vs expected* and ask. This is the executable-requirements contract, not a style preference.
- **Shared code is a single source of truth.** After editing anything under `shared/`, run `npm run sync-shared` to regenerate the vendored `*.GENERATED.mjs` copies in `server/src/vendor/` and `extension/vendor/`, and commit them; the root drift guard (`dev/build/tools/test/shared-drift.test.mjs`) fails on any byte divergence.

## Make & propose a change

- **Lifecycle (from the corpus, enforced by the `task-lifecycle` check):** open a GitHub issue → develop on a branch → reference the issue in commits (`Refs/Fixes/Closes #N`) → open a PR. The advanced git/GitHub procedures (commit layering, CI-trigger rules, recovering after a squash-merge) are the `git-github-advanced` skill.
- **Definition of done:** `npm run test:all` is green; any `shared/` edit is followed by `sync-shared` + committed generated copies; an intentional UI change has refreshed goldens and a matching requirement/case; a public API change follows the additive-only versioning policy ([architecture](../docs/architecture.md) §9.1); nothing owner-specific or generated-but-uncommitted is left dangling (see [Continuity](#continuity--handoff)).
- **Releasing is version-driven and mostly automatic** — the user-visible version is `extension/manifest.json`'s `version`; merging a bump to `main` cuts the GitHub Release and the daily auto-release ships shipped-file changes to the Chrome Web Store. Touch the release workflows **only** when cutting/publishing a release — this repo's instance of the shared chrome-extension-release standard (the canon guide in Claudinite owns the cross-repo contract and manual store procedures).

=== chrome-extension.md
# Chrome extension (MV3) — lessons

Notes for the TLDR extension under `extension/`. These are largely portable; the distilled, project-stripped
versions are what would propagate to the corpus `technologies/chrome-extension.md`.

- **Escalate to interactive auth only from a real user gesture, and only as a last resort.** Reads send no
  token, so the panel-open/read path can't prompt. The write path must too: the first POST uses a
  silent-only token, and a *visible* Google prompt is permitted **only** on the 401 retry — which already
  runs inside the Post click. Encode it as a hard rule: `getIdToken` escalates to interactive **iff**
  `interactive && forceRefresh` (both default false), so no other caller can surface UI by accident. Worked
  example: `extension/src/auth.mjs` (`getIdToken` escalation guard) + `extension/src/api.mjs` (`postComment`
  silent-first, interactive-on-401). Unit-tested by stubbing `chrome.*` in `extension-test/auth.test.mjs`.

- **A toolbar action can't left-click-OPEN and left-click-CLOSE from one static manifest, and a popup
  suppresses `onClicked` entirely — so gate the popup, don't make it permanent.** MV3 has no
  is-open/close API and a `default_popup` swallows every click before `onClicked` fires. To make a plain
  click just open (pane closed) or close (pane open) the side panel — without a category picker popping
  up each time — track pane-open via the panel's `Port` and keep the popup **cleared** (`setPopup({popup:''})`)
  except on genuine first run: no category chosen yet AND no pane open. The first-run popup then gives way
  the instant a category lands in `storage.local`, reconciled from a `storage.onChanged` listener (not
  just the panel's Port connect), so it clears whether the category was picked from the popup or the
  right-click menu. Move the "which category" choice to the icon's **right-click** menu:
  `chrome.contextMenus.create({contexts:['action'], …})` puts items on the toolbar icon itself, and
  `contextMenus` carries **no** install-time warning. Recreate the items with `removeAll()` first on
  install/startup so they self-heal instead of throwing on duplicate ids. Worked example:
  `extension/src/service-worker.mjs` (`reflectPopup`/`hasChosenCategory`, the `onClicked` open-or-close,
  `setupCategoryContextMenu` + its `onClicked`, and the `storage.onChanged` first-run reconcile).

- **A registered/declarative content script is a CLASSIC script — it can't be an ES module, so top-level
  `import`s throw *in the host page*, silently.** `chrome.scripting.registerContentScripts` (and static
  `content_scripts`) inject their `js` files as classic scripts; there is no module mode
  (`RegisteredContentScript` has no `type: 'module'`, unlike a page's `<script type="module">`). Point one
  at a file that starts with `import { … } from './x.mjs'` and Chrome throws `Uncaught SyntaxError: Cannot
  use import statement outside a module` — but in the **third-party page's** console, not the extension's
  service-worker/side-panel devtools, so the feature looks like a total no-op with a clean extension
  console. This bit the link-hover preview: `link-hover.mjs` was modeled on `sidepanel.mjs` (which is fine
  as a module — `sidepanel.html` loads it via `<script type="module">`) and registered directly, so the
  toggle worked, the permission was granted, and nothing ever rendered. Fix WITHOUT a bundler (this repo
  ships raw modules): register a tiny **classic loader** whose only statement is a *dynamic*
  `import(chrome.runtime.getURL('src/link-hover.mjs'))` — dynamic `import()` is legal in a classic script,
  and the module it pulls in runs in the same content-script isolated world with the content-script
  `chrome.*` surface (storage, `runtime.sendMessage`) intact. The dynamically-imported module **and its
  whole transitive import graph** must be listed in `web_accessible_resources` (gated to the feature's
  origins) or the fetch is blocked; a unit test walks that graph from the entry module so a newly-added
  import can't silently fall out of the list. Worked example: `extension/src/link-hover-loader.mjs` (the
  injected classic loader) + `extension/manifest.json` (`web_accessible_resources`) +
  `extension-test/manifest.test.mjs` (the graph-coverage + classic-loader guards). NB the jsdom harness
  (`dev/requirements/shared/render/link-hover-harness.mjs`) `import()`s `link-hover.mjs` directly, so it
  proves the module's *logic* but never Chrome's classic-injection contract — exactly the seam this bug
  lived in (the `11.14` real-Chrome e2e is the tracked gap).

- **A "single-source vendoring / `*.GENERATED.mjs`" pack** — homed by `basics` (`generated-merge-driver`), and the one deterministic rule ("re-run `sync-shared` after editing `shared/`") is already enforced by the repo's own `dev/build/tools/test/shared-drift.test.mjs` in root `npm test`. Nothing left to carry.
- **A "deterministic UI rendering" pack** (locale/TZ/font pinning) — homed by `executable-requirements` §"Determinism or it isn't spec" + "Rendering recipes per stack"; `locale-guard.mjs` is this repo's implementation of that canon rule, not new knowledge.
- **A "monorepo without npm workspaces" facet** (four un-linked `package.json`s chained by `npm --prefix` in `test:all`, path-filtered per-package CI lanes) — genuine and project-shaped, but I could ground exactly one statement about it (the chain in root `package.json`), which is inferable from the file itself. One inferable rule doesn't mint a pack, and there's no gotcha the repo has actually paid for.
- **The dev/prod two-account runbook** — project-specific and genuine, but a single rule in territory adjacent to `local/tldr`; adding to an existing local pack is growth-extract's job, not this task's, and a lone rule doesn't mint a pack.

No candidate cleared "a technology or domain the canon doesn't home, with several durable **work** rules". Nothing was authored — padding a pack to have something to ship is the failure this task names.

### 3. Standing note — still unactioned (third run running)

**This repo should declare the canon `aws-sam` pack** rather than growing a local one. Unchanged since 2026-07-26 and 2026-08-02: `.claudinite-checks.json` still doesn't declare it and the mount still doesn't carry it. Declaring an id the mount doesn't know is a settings error, so this wants the `adopt-pack` flow (declare → interview → re-vendor → land), not a hand-edit of the declaration list. It is outside this task's write scope (`.claudinite/local/packs/` only), so it needs a separate dispatch or an owner action.

**Method flag, restated:** step 2 calls `.claudinite/shared/packs/` "the canon shelf", but it is the *declared subset* plus the `requires` closure (`git-github` is present only because `basics` requires it). A technology can look unhomed there purely because its canon pack was never declared — the `aws-sam` trap.

2	import { classificationLine, classesIn } from '../../../shared/engine/checks/helpers/session-transcript.mjs';
3	
4	// The testable half of RULES.md's "Put the `Comment class:` line on its own
5	// line": the classifier reads the WHOLE classification line and adds EVERY class
6	// token it finds (`classesIn()` matches globally), so the natural-sounding
7	//     Comment class: other — not a correction, feature request, or process-change
8	// declares all four classes, not `other`. The stray `feature` then arms
9	// `feature-requirements-first` BLOCKING against whatever commits the branch
10	// carries, even when the session never touched a product feature.
11	//
12	// This asserts the MANDATED FORM, not the author's intent. The prose tells the
13	// agent to write the class alone and put any explanation on the next line, so
14	// the line either is that or it is not — a question every character of it
15	// answers. An earlier draft chased intent instead, firing only on a class token
16	// that followed a negation word from a hand-picked list ("not", "never",
17	// "besides", …). That is unbounded in the wrong direction: the harm comes from a
18	// class token being PRESENT, and prose smuggles them in without negating
19	// anything. Probed against the real helper, that draft stayed silent on
20	//     Comment class: other — unrelated to any feature request      (declares feature)
21	//     Comment class: other, setting the feature question aside     (declares feature)
22	//     Comment class: correction | feature | process-change | other (declares all four)
23	// — the last a verbatim paste of the menu out of the classifier's own prompt,
24	// i.e. the likeliest way this bug is reproduced, missed by the check named for
25	// it. Checking the form catches all three and needs no word list, because a
26	// conforming line has nowhere to hide a token.
27	//
28	// A genuinely mixed comment stays legal and stays silent: it names each part it
29	// really is, positively, on that one line (`Comment class: correction,
30	// process-change`). Whether four comma-separated classes are "honest" is exactly
31	// the intent judgment this rule refuses to make — the form is respected, so the
32	// classifier does what the line asked.
33	//
34	// ADVISORY, deliberately, where the underlying defect is blocking-grade: the
35	// transcript is append-only, so by the time this is observable the declaration
36	// cannot be retracted. A blocking finding could never converge — it would spend
37	// the session's Stop cycles on something no edit can fix, which is precisely the
38	// waste the lesson records. Its job is to name the cause the moment it appears
39	// so the session doesn't re-derive it from an unexplained
40	// `feature-requirements-first` failure.
41	
42	// One class token, spelled as the classifier's own alternation spells it, so
43	// this check models what `classesIn()` sees rather than a second opinion of it.
44	const CLASS = String.raw`(?:correction|feature|process[\s-]change|other)`;
45	// The mandated form: class tokens joined by a declaration separator, nothing
46	// else. `|` is deliberately NOT a separator — it is how the prompt renders the
47	// menu, so pasting the menu verbatim fails this pattern rather than reading as
48	// a four-class declaration.
49	const CONFORMING_RE = new RegExp(String.raw`^\s*${CLASS}(?:\s*(?:,|&|\+|and)\s*${CLASS})*\s*\.?\s*$`, 'i');
50	
51	const rule = {
52	  id: 'tldr/comment-class-menu',
53	  severity: 'advisory',
54	  description: 'The `Comment class:` line must carry the class alone — every class token on it is declared, however the line phrases them',
55	  doc: '.claudinite/local/packs/tldr/RULES.md',
56	  scope: 'work',
57	  why: 'the classifier adds every class token on the classification line, so any explanation sharing that line declares the classes it mentions — a stray `feature` arms feature-requirements-first BLOCKING against the branch even when no product feature was touched',
58	
59	  run(work) {
60	    // Only the latest owner turn is judged, for the same reason
61	    // comment-classification judges only that one: the transcript is
62	    // append-only, so an earlier turn's line was already reported at its own
63	    // Stop and can never converge.
64	    const turn = work.conversation().ownerTurns().last();
65	    if (!turn.exists) return [];
66	    const line = classificationLine(turn.reply());
67	    // No classification line at all is comment-classification's finding, not this one.
68	    if (!line) return [];
69	
70	    // Everything after the `Comment class:` colon — the prefix cannot contain
71	    // one (the helper's pattern forbids it), so the first colon is the split.
72	    const declaration = line.slice(line.indexOf(':') + 1);
73	    if (CONFORMING_RE.test(declaration)) return [];
74	
75	    const declared = [...classesIn(declaration)].sort();
76	    // A line naming no class at all is unclassified — comment-classification's
77	    // finding, not this one.
78	    if (!declared.length) return [];
79	
80	    const arms = declared.includes('feature')
81	      ? ', including `feature`, which arms `feature-requirements-first` BLOCKING against this branch'
82	      : '';
83	
84	    return [finding(rule, {
85	      file: '(conversation)',
86	      what: `the \`Comment class:\` line carries more than the class it means, so the classifier reads it as declaring ${declared.map((c) => `\`${c}\``).join(', ')}${arms}`,
87	      fix: 'write the class alone on its own line — `Comment class: other` — and put any explanation on the NEXT line; a genuinely mixed comment names each part it really is, comma-separated, on that one line. The transcript is append-only, so re-declaring cleanly on a later line does not override this one — do not retry, and expect the declared classes\' rules to fire on this branch',
88	    })];
89	  },
90	};

input.title: Adopt the canon packs this repo's stack matches but never declared: `aws-sam` and `google-identity`
input.body:
Handoff from the weekly `growth-discover-packs` routine (standing log: #122). That task's write scope is `.claudinite/local/packs/` only, and adoption re-vendors the read-only mount — so it can note this but never do it. This issue exists so the note converges instead of being re-derived every week: it has now been raised on **2026-07-26, 2026-08-02, 2026-08-09 and 2026-08-16** with no action.

## What is missing

Two canon packs are matched by this repo's real files (both are *fingerprinted* packs — the fingerprint only suspects, declaring is still the project's call) and are declared nowhere in `.claudinite-checks.json`, so neither is vendored into `.claudinite/shared/packs/` and neither contributes prose, checks or skills to any session:

| Pack | Fingerprint (per `packs/directory.GENERATED.md`) | This repo's matching evidence |
|---|---|---|
| `aws-sam` | a SAM template (`template.yaml`/`.yml`) | `server/template.yaml` (`Transform: AWS::Serverless-2016-10-31`), `server/samconfig.toml`, `sam build` / `sam validate --lint` in `server/package.json`, `aws-actions/setup-sam@v3` in `deploy.yml` and `test-server.yml`, the `Metadata.BuildMethod: esbuild` bundling block |
| `google-identity` | a backend validating Google Sign-In ID tokens (a JWT authorizer / OIDC verifier with the Google accounts issuer) | `server/template.yaml` `CommentsApi.Auth.Authorizers.GoogleJwt` — `issuer: https://accounts.google.com`, `audience: [!Ref GoogleClientId]` with `AllowedPattern: '.+'` so it can never be empty — plus the `email_verified` claim checks in `server/src/handler.mjs` (lines 127, 200) |

`google-identity` has not been raised on #122 before; the previous three runs named only `aws-sam`. It surfaced now because `packs/directory.GENERATED.md` — the catalog of *every* canon pack — only arrived in the mount on 2026-08-12 (#236). Before that, runs could only see `.claudinite/shared/packs/`, which is the **declared subset**, not the shelf.

The client half of Google auth (`extension/src/auth.mjs` — `launchWebAuthFlow`, `response_type=id_token`, `nonce`, `prompt=none`, `login_hint`) is already homed by the declared `chrome-extension` pack. What is unhomed is the **server-side validation** half: audience pinning, issuer, `email_verified`.

## What breaks while this is off

- Rules for the SAM/Lambda/API-Gateway/DynamoDB layer and for server-side ID-token validation never load, so every session touching `server/` re-derives them or misses them. That layer carries this product's entire write-auth boundary (`architecture.md` §6.3: "the security boundary is the JWT authorizer, never browser CORS"), and an audience or issuer mistake there is a silent, total auth bypass.
- `dev/procedures/aws-sam.md` already states its portable subsets "now live in the canon `aws-sam` pack" — so this repo's own doc points at a pack that isn't loaded. The pointer reads as covered when nothing covers it.

## Do not fix it by editing the declaration list

Declaring an id the mounted registry does not know is a **blocking** settings error, not a no-op — `check_the_world.mjs` builds `knownIds` from the *discovered* (i.e. vendored) packs and emits `declares unknown pack "<name>"` for anything else, which turns `Claudinite conformance` red on every PR and push. The declaration and the re-vendor have to land together, which is what the `adopt-pack` skill does (declare → adoption interview → re-vendor → scaffold).

## Steps

- [ ] Run `adopt-pack` for `aws-sam` (it declares, runs the pack's adoption questions, re-vendors, scaffolds).
- [ ] Run `adopt-pack` for `google-identity`.
- [ ] Confirm `.claudinite/shared/packs/aws-sam/` and `.claudinite/shared/packs/google-identity/` are present and `node .claudinite/shared/engine/checks/check_the_world.mjs` reports **0 blocking**.
- [ ] Reconcile `dev/procedures/aws-sam.md` against the newly-mounted pack — strip what the canon now homes, keep only this repo's residue (the frozen base-table `KeySchema`, the two-account dev/prod OIDC split, environment derived from `stack_name`). That is the `growth-dedup` skill's job, not this one's.

## Closing condition

Both packs are declared in `.claudinite-checks.json`, both are vendored in the mount, and `check_the_world.mjs` is green. Anything short of that — e.g. a declaration landed without the re-vendor — leaves the repo worse than it is today, so do not close on a partial.

---

## 2026-08-16 (w2026-08-16, issue #270)

**Nothing new worth a local pack this run.** No pack authored, no PR opened.

**What is new this run:** the shelf comparison could finally be done against the *real* shelf, and it turned up a **second** undeclared canon pack — `google-identity` — that the previous three runs could not see. The thrice-repeated "should declare `aws-sam`" note has been escalated out of this log into its own converging issue, **#282**.

### 1. Manifest — this repo's stack, from its files

#### Technologies

- **Node.js / ESM, `node --test` as the whole toolchain** — *evidence:* `"type": "module"` in all four `package.json`s (root, `extension/`, `server/`, `dev/`); every `test` script is `node --test`; root `test:all` chains the four suites with `npm --prefix`. *What it is here:* the only runtime and the only test runner — no bundler for the extension, no linter. *Prominence:* core.
- **Chrome extension, MV3** — *evidence:* `extension/manifest.json` (`manifest_version: 3`, `"type": "module"` service worker, `side_panel`, `action.default_popup`, `options_ui`, `optional_host_permissions`, `web_accessible_resources`, `minimum_chrome_version: 116`); ~21 modules under `extension/src/`. *What it is here:* the client product. *Prominence:* core.
- **AWS SAM / CloudFormation** — *evidence:* `server/template.yaml` (`Transform: AWS::Serverless-2016-10-31`), `server/samconfig.toml`, `sam build` / `sam validate --lint` in `server/package.json`, `aws-actions/setup-sam@v3` in `deploy.yml` + `test-server.yml`. *What it is here:* the backend's IaC and build. *Prominence:* core.
- **AWS Lambda `nodejs22.x` + API Gateway HTTP API v2 + a Google JWT authorizer** — *evidence:* `template.yaml` `Globals.Function`, `CommentsApi.Auth.Authorizers.GoogleJwt`, five routes opting into `Auth` individually (both GETs public by design). *What it is here:* the entire server tier and its auth boundary. *Prominence:* core.
- **DynamoDB, single table** — *evidence:* `CommentsTable` + the sparse `CategoryRankIndex` GSI, TTL on `expiresAt`, PITR, SSE, `DeletionPolicy`/`UpdateReplacePolicy: Retain`, table name derived from `AWS::StackName` through the `IsProd` condition; `@aws-sdk/client-dynamodb` + `@aws-sdk/lib-dynamodb` + `ulid`; `aws-sdk-client-mock` in tests. *Prominence:* core.
- **esbuild** — *evidence:* `server/package.json` dependency, driven by `template.yaml` `Metadata.BuildMethod: esbuild` (cjs, node22, minify, sourcemap, `External: []` so the SDK is bundled). *Prominence:* supporting. *Cross-note:* also a deployment concern (artifact determinism).
- **jsdom + satori + `@resvg/resvg-js` + pixelmatch + pngjs** — *evidence:* `dev/package.json` devDependencies; `dev/requirements/shared/render/` with vendored Liberation fonts; `TZ=UTC LANG=C.UTF-8` pinned in the `dev` scripts + `locale-guard.mjs`. *What it is here:* the deterministic render harness behind the golden-image kinds. *Prominence:* core.
- **The executable-requirements suite** — *evidence:* `dev/requirements/` with six kind folders (`behavior`, `component`, `dom`, `logic`, `server`, `shared`), `<slug>.<n>.<m>.case.mjs` naming, `requirements.md`, `requirements-coverage.test.mjs`, `gallery.test.mjs`. *Prominence:* core.
- **GitHub Actions** — *evidence:* 12 workflows + 3 composite actions (`bump-extension-patch`, `read-release-config`, `report-failure`). *Prominence:* core.
- **Byte-identical source vendoring** — *evidence:* `dev/build/tools/sync-shared.mjs` (the `SHARED` list) fanning `shared/normalizeUrl.mjs` + `shared/categories.mjs` into `server/src/vendor/` and `extension/vendor/` as `*.GENERATED.mjs`, guarded by `dev/build/tools/test/shared-drift.test.mjs` and `.gitattributes` (`linguist-generated merge=ours`). *Prominence:* core.
- **The vendored Claudinite engine** — *evidence:* `.claudinite/shared/` mount, `.claude/settings.json` hooks, `.claudinite-checks.json` declaring 13 pack entries + the `barriers` and `sharedConstants` config. *Prominence:* core.
- **`dev/build/tools/gen-icons.mjs`** — *evidence:* zlib-only placeholder icon generator; its own header says "replace `icons/` with real branding before a Chrome Web Store submission"; wired into no script or workflow; #17 tracks replacing the output. *Prominence:* vestigial `?`.
- **`server/scripts/seed-dev.mjs`** — *evidence:* dev-table seeding with a hard prod-table refusal; run by hand only. *Prominence:* supporting.

#### External services / APIs

- **Google Identity / OAuth "Web application" client** — *evidence:* client half in `extension/src/auth.mjs` (`launchWebAuthFlow`, `response_type=id_token`, `nonce` verification, `prompt=none`, `login_hint`); server half in `template.yaml` (`issuer: https://accounts.google.com`, `audience: [!Ref GoogleClientId]`, `AllowedPattern: '.+'`) plus `email_verified` claim checks in `server/src/handler.mjs:127,200`. *What it is here:* the sole identity provider and the whole write-auth boundary. *Prominence:* core.
- **AWS, `il-central-1`, two separate accounts (dev + prod)** — *evidence:* `samconfig.toml` (both envs), `deploy.yml`'s `AWS_DEPLOY_ROLE_ARN` / `AWS_DEV_DEPLOY_ROLE_ARN` split, `dev/docs/dev-account-runbook.md`. *Prominence:* core.
- **GitHub OIDC → AWS** — *evidence:* `permissions: id-token: write` + `aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@v6` in `deploy.yml` and the read-only `aws-status.yml`; no stored keys. *Prominence:* core.
- **Chrome Web Store API** — *evidence:* `chrome-extension-publish-store.yml`. *Prominence:* core.

{"number":282,"title":"Adopt the canon packs this repo's stack matches but never declared: `aws-sam` and `google-identity`","body":"Handoff from the weekly `growth-discover-packs` routine (standing log: #122). That task's write scope is `.claudinite/local/packs/` only, and adoption re-vendors the read-only mount — so it can note this but never do it. This issue exists so the note converges instead of being re-derived every week: it has now been raised on **2026-07-26, 2026-08-02, 2026-08-09 and 2026-08-16** with no action.

## What is missing

Two canon packs are matched by this repo's real files (both are *fingerprinted* packs — the fingerprint only suspects, declaring is still the project's call) and are declared nowhere in `.claudinite-checks.json`, so neither is vendored into `.claudinite/shared/packs/` and neither contributes prose, checks or skills to any session:

| Pack | Fingerprint (per `packs/directory.GENERATED.md`) | This repo's matching evidence |
|---|---|---|
| `aws-sam` | a SAM template (`template.yaml`/`.yml`) | `server/template.yaml` (`Transform: AWS::Serverless-2016-10-31`), `server/samconfig.toml`, `sam build` / `sam validate --lint` in `server/package.json`, `aws-actions/setup-sam@v3` in `deploy.yml` and `test-server.yml`, the `Metadata.BuildMethod: esbuild` bundling block |
| `google-identity` | a backend validating Google Sign-In ID tokens (a JWT authorizer / OIDC verifier with the Google accounts issuer) | `server/template.yaml` `CommentsApi.Auth.Authorizers.GoogleJwt` — `issuer: https://accounts.google.com`, `audience: [!Ref GoogleClientId]` with `AllowedPattern: '.+'` so it can never be empty — plus the `email_verified` claim checks in `server/src/handler.mjs` (lines 127, 200) |

`google-identity` has not been raised on #122 before; the previous three runs named only `aws-sam`. It surfaced now because `packs/directory.GENERATED.md` — the catalog of *every* canon pack — only arrived in the mount on 2026-08-12 (#236). Before that, runs could only see `.claudinite/shared/packs/`, which is the **declared subset**, not the shelf.

The client half of Google auth (`extension/src/auth.mjs` — `launchWebAuthFlow`, `response_type=id_token`, `nonce`, `prompt=none`, `login_hint`) is already homed by the declared `chrome-extension` pack. What is unhomed is the **server-side validation** half: audience pinning, issuer, `email_verified`.

## What breaks while this is off

- Rules for the SAM/Lambda/API-Gateway/DynamoDB layer and for server-side ID-token validation never load, so every session touching `server/` re-derives them or misses them. That layer carries this product's entire write-auth boundary (`architecture.md` §6.3: "the security boundary is the JWT authorizer, never browser CORS"), and an audience or issuer mistake there is a silent, total auth bypass.
- `dev/procedures/aws-sam.md` already states its portable subsets "now live in the canon `aws-sam` pack" — so this repo's own doc points at a pack that isn't loaded. The pointer reads as covered when nothing covers it.

## Do not fix it by editing the declaration list

Declaring an id the mounted registry does not know is a **blocking** settings error, not a no-op — `check_the_world.mjs` builds `knownIds` from the *discovered* (i.e. vendored) packs and emits `declares unknown pack ""` for anything else, which turns `Claudinite conformance` red on every PR and push. The declaration and the re-vendor have to land together, which is what the `adopt-pack` skill does (declare → adoption interview → re-vendor → scaffold).

## Steps

- [ ] Run `adopt-pack` for `aws-sam` (it declares, runs the pack's adoption questions, re-vendors, scaffolds).
- [ ] Run `adopt-pack` for `google-identity`.
- [ ] Confirm `.claudinite/shared/packs/aws-sam/` and `.claudinite/shared/packs/google-identity/` are present and `node .claudinite/shared/engine/checks/check_the_world.mjs` reports **0 blocking**.
